**Release candidate for 0.4.7.** Barring something found in testing, this is what 0.4.7 will be. Still a pre-release: not marked Latest. If you want a stable build, use v0.4.6.

Linux x86_64 only — pre-releases ship the tarball. No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews.

If you have been flying the alphas and betas, the changes since beta.2 are small: three configuration settings that never did anything have been removed. **If you are coming from 0.4.6, read the two upgrade sections below before your first flight** — both describe expected behaviour that looks like a regression if you are not expecting it.

---

## What 0.4.7 is about

One symptom, three causes. XEarthLayer's memory grew steadily on long flights until the system killed it — a 12-hour flight ended at 64 GB against a configured 4 GB cache.

**None of it was a leak.** Bytes actually in use stayed flat at 572–725 MB across an eighteen-fold increase in work; everything was being freed. What grew was glibc's *retention* of freed memory, which is why nothing in the code ever looked wrong.

glibc gives each thread a heap arena, and returns memory only by trimming the **top** of one. Space stranded below a live allocation stays committed for the life of the process, so an arena grows to cover the worst burst it ever saw and never gives it back. The total is the sum of every arena's personal high-water mark — and with a ceiling of eight arenas per core, every traffic burst could recruit *fresh* arenas that had never seen a peak. Rare peaks were being converted into permanent floor, once per arena.

Three fixes, one per mechanism: pin the threshold that decides whether a tile comes from an arena at all, size the thread pool from actual work rather than accepting the 512-thread default, and cap the arena count so the total converges.

Measured over a matched 11-hour flight: committed memory **11,580 → 9,687 MB**, arena **6,091 → 4,038 MB**, swap **1,063 → 533 MB**, and growth steps after initial sizing **18 → 1**. Throughput was unchanged at 3.03 vs 3.06 textures/second.

These fixes are Linux-only. macOS uses a different allocator and is unaffected — and, for now, unprotected.

---

## Upgrading from 0.4.6: expect one slower flight

0.4.7-alpha.1 corrected how mipmaps are written into generated textures, which changed their size. **Every texture cached by 0.4.6 is therefore the wrong size for this build.**

Until this release those were detected at the last moment, replaced with a magenta placeholder, and — because nothing deleted them — served as magenta again on every subsequent request. Permanently, with no way back short of clearing the cache by hand.

They are now replaced properly the first time they are read. The cost is that your first flight after upgrading regenerates a large part of the texture cache: more downloading, more encoding, and more placeholder tiles than usual while it catches up. It settles after that.

## The placeholder timeout is now the documented 10 seconds

When a texture cannot be produced in time, XEarthLayer serves a magenta placeholder rather than making the simulator wait. That limit is `generation.timeout`, documented and reported as 10 seconds — but the setting never reached the code, which used a hardcoded 30.

It is now honoured. This is the value the documentation has always claimed, but it is a real change: the window before a placeholder appears is three times shorter than in 0.4.6. Combined with the cache refill above, the first flight after upgrading is where you are most likely to notice it. If you would rather have the old behaviour while the cache warms, set `timeout = 30` under `[generation]` and put it back afterwards.

---

## A corrupt cache file could stop XEarthLayer starting

Found by a tester on beta.1, who could not start at all:

```
memory allocation of 3418906639127570548 bytes failed
Aborted (core dumped)
```

That number is not a quantity of memory. In hexadecimal it is `0x2f726579616c6874`, which read as text is `thlayer/` — eight characters of the path `~/.xearthlayer/`. A damaged byte in the index cache had shifted every later read along by one position, so part of a file path was read as a field saying how many bytes to allocate.

The code already intended to handle this: read the cache, and if the read fails, throw it away and rebuild. That was correct, and it had never once run — a failed allocation of that size terminates the process rather than reporting an error the surrounding code can catch.

Every cache now bounds what it reads by the size of the file it is reading, writes durably so an interrupted write cannot leave a half-finished file behind, and discards anything it cannot trust. A cache that cannot be read is regenerated, which is what a cache is for.

## Three settings that never did anything have been removed

`executor.network_concurrent`, `executor.cpu_concurrent` and `executor.disk_io_concurrent` were reported by `config list` but never reached the executor. Worse, `config list` printed values from a second formula that disagreed with the one actually in use — on a 32-thread machine it reported a CPU capacity of 16 while the executor ran 40.

Resource pool sizes are derived from your processor and are no longer configurable. The figures involved are tuned by flight testing and are load-bearing for the memory work above, so exposing them as settings was a way to undo it by accident.

Your configuration will still load if it contains these keys. `xearthlayer config upgrade` removes them. Nothing about how XEarthLayer runs changes — the values were never used.

## Also fixed

**The whole world could be marked as having no scenery.** Prefetch retires a region when there is no scenery to fetch there. With no scenery index loaded, the check returned "nothing here" — indistinguishable from having looked and genuinely found nothing — so regions were retired without anything being consulted. ([#228](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/228))

**`xearthlayer diagnostics` could hang forever.** Measuring the cache directory walked the entire tree; on a multi-terabyte cache it never finished, so the report never printed — and since the bug report form asks for that output, this stopped people filing bugs at all. Now bounded at five seconds. ([#251](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/251), reported by [@mmaechtel](https://github.com/mmaechtel))

**Two more ignored settings.** `cache.dds_disk_ratio` never reached the cache, which always split its disk budget 60/40 regardless of the setting while the dashboard displayed your figure. And `executor.max_concurrent_jobs` had moved section in an earlier release without the reader following, so a configuration XEarthLayer wrote itself could not be read back. ([#248](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/248), reported by [@mmaechtel](https://github.com/mmaechtel))

---

## Reporting

`xearthlayer diagnostics` now completes, so please include it. The log at `~/.xearthlayer/xearthlayer.log` is overwritten on every launch — copy it aside before relaunching if you hit something worth reporting.

Most useful for this candidate:

- Whether the first flight after upgrading from 0.4.6 settles as described, and roughly how long it takes.
- Long flights. The memory work is the reason this release exists, and the only way to falsify it is hours in the air.
